instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.66 bars anyone from lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under § 13.63, and § 13.63(1)(a) provides for the lobbyist licensing application/issuance requirement.
A lobbyist license 'shall expire on December 31 of each even-numbered year,' i.e., on a biennial (2-year) cycle.
Lobbyists must obtain a license under § 13.63, principals must file a registration statement under § 13.64, and a separate written authorization must be filed for each principal under § 13.65.
Section 13.621(3) exempts elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees from specified lobbying provisions 'when acting in an official capacity.'

Section 13.621(2) provides that an agency filing a statement under § 13.695 and named officials are not subject to several lobbying requirements, 'except as provided in s. 13.695,' creating a partial exemption.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled sections specify amendment/update deadlines for agency statements (§ 13.695(2)) and topic reports (§ 13.67(1)), but do not state any general deadline for lobbyists to amend/ update their own license application/registration information.

The statute requires licensure and authorization before engaging in lobbying (§ 13.66; § 13.65), not a deadline measured in days after first lobbying; no 'days after first lobbying' registration deadline appears in the provided text.
The provided license application provisions (§ 13.63(1)(a)) list required identifiers (e.g., SSN) but do not address whether a photograph must be submitted.
